meta.triageRationale: One cohesive story with real design choices and multiple build tasks, but no new subsystem: the approval path already exists end-to-end (workflow.approve RPC -> approveWorkflowTarget in src/workflow/gates.ts -> artifact store) and already withholds on missing/same-party/stale reviews (ReviewBlockedError). What is missing is the human-gate layer at code level: no record of insrc_present, no per-artifact attestation, batch epicHash approval, and the RPC is callable by any raw socket client. That is a design decision (present-token binding + caller/attestation requirements in the shared approve path) across daemon + workflow + MCP + tests — feature tier: standalone LLD -> plan -> build, not an epic.

The JSON contains a triage rationale and mappings labelled ac1–ac6, without the criteria's text. The workflow run log records stage events only. findings.premise: Presentation currently reads pending artifacts without recording presentation, while MCP approval and the IDE decision path delegate to shared workflow approval code.
findings.evidence: handleInsrcPresent calls pendingWorkflow, selects names with exactly one match, and returns { presented, notPending } without writing. handleWorkflowApprove forwards through approveWorkflow to workflow.approve; that handler calls approveWorkflowTarget. handleReviewDecision also calls approveWorkflowTarget for approval. [files: src/mcp/server.ts, src/mcp/daemon-stream.ts, src/daemon/handler-runtime.ts, src/workflow/review-decision.ts, src/workflow/gates.ts]
findings.action: Retain these delegation boundaries when adding persistence and enforcement.

findings.premise: BUILD freshness honors the overrideReview escape described in §4 and reference c1.
findings.evidence: approveArtifactOwned calls assertFreshBuildReview before evaluating overrideReview. enforceCodeReviewGate likewise returns stale-review before applying enforcement or override settings. The MCP description explicitly says stale fingerprinted identity withholds approval 'even with overrides or enforcement off'. The design's combined invariant and c1 description incorrectly imply that freshness is overridable. [files: src/workflow/gates.ts, src/workflow/code-review/gate.ts, src/mcp/server.ts, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103d5d33994/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Distinguish overridable legacy review failures from non-overridable fingerprint freshness failures, and explicitly preserve the latter.

findings.premise: Presentation persistence is new, while the proposed name-resolution semantics already exist.
findings.evidence: Source searches found no recordPresentations, requireFreshPresentation, workflow.present or proposed presentation metadata fields. Existing namesPending compares artifact IDs case-insensitively and accepts exact or suffix document paths; handleInsrcPresent requires exactly one match. Existing tests exercise duplicate inputs, ambiguous paths, case differences and document-less records. [files: src/mcp/server.ts, src/mcp/__tests__/present-dispatch.test.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/review-presenter.ts]
findings.action: Reuse the established matching semantics and preserve original declared names in the MCP presented response even if the daemon returns canonical artifact IDs.

findings.premise: Adding presentation metadata can leave BUILD review fingerprinting untouched.
findings.evidence: BUILD_APPROVAL_IDENTITY_EXCLUSIONS contains exactly ['approvedAt', 'rejectedAt', 'rejectReason', 'reviewOverride']. canonicalReviewBuild retains all other metadata, and readReviewInputSnapshot hashes that result into buildDigest. Therefore stamping presentedAt/presentedBy/presentationToken after review changes the reviewed identity; compareReviewInputFingerprint returns mismatch and approval fails. Re-review followed by re-presentation repeats the problem. These fingerprint and rollback contracts are absent from the change inventory. [files: src/workflow/code-review/input-fingerprint.ts, src/workflow/gates.ts, src/workflow/code-review/gate.ts, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103d5d33994/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Design how presentation and consumption audit fields interact with fingerprint identity, existing stored fingerprints and approval rollback. Add a regression using a real fingerprinted BUILD through review→present→approve while retaining detection of material changes.

findings.premise: The RPC and MCP contract change inventory is complete.
findings.evidence: src/mcp/daemon-stream.ts declares approveWorkflow's request with repo, artifactPath, epicHash and overrideReview only; this transport signature is omitted. Every daemon method also has an explicit entry in threads/method-class.ts, enforced against runtime handler tables by method-class.test.ts. The design lists only handler-runtime.ts for workflow.present. MCP registration currently advertises insrc_present as readOnlyHint:true and idempotentHint:true, which conflicts with refreshing a random token on every call. [files: src/mcp/daemon-stream.ts, src/mcp/server.ts, src/daemon/threads/method-class.ts, src/daemon/threads/__tests__/method-class.test.ts, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103d5d33994/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Include transport types/helpers, method classification and registry tests, registered input schemas, and updated presentation annotations/descriptions in the explicit change sites.

findings.premise: IDE and TUI presentation wiring can remain an optional compatibility follow-up after enabling the gate by default.
findings.evidence: VS Code content loading calls workflow.artifactContent and its decision action calls workflow.reviewDecision. JetBrains approve calls workflow.approve. Neither client contains workflow.present. The TUI calls src/cli/services/workflow.ts::approve, which directly invokes approveArtifactByJsonPath rather than approveWorkflowTarget. Thus the default-on lower-level gate would withhold existing approval actions after documents are opened unless a separate MCP presentation happened first. The design identifies this dependency but leaves its delivery unresolved. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/docs-review-client.ts, jetbrains-plugin/src/main/kotlin/ai/insors/insrc/jetbrains/daemon/DaemonGateway.kt, src/cli/services/workflow.ts, src/cli/panes/WorkflowsPane.tsx, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103d5d33994/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Make presentation wiring for both current IDE clients and the TUI a required rollout dependency. Specify successful presentation, expiry/re-presentation and write-error behavior for each approval surface.

findings.premise: AMD records fit the proposed ApprovableArtifactMeta storage and shared approval model.
findings.evidence: AmendmentRecord is flat, with top-level status/approvedAt/approvedBy and no meta. listPendingArtifacts explicitly handles AMD using art.status === 'pending'. approveAmendment writes status:'approved' through its separate transition function, and the TUI invokes that writer directly. Adding meta presentation fields and gating approveArtifactByJsonPath neither gates this real amendment approval path nor updates AMD status correctly. [files: src/workflow/amendments/types.ts, src/workflow/amendments/store.ts, src/workflow/pending.ts, src/cli/services/workflow.ts, src/cli/panes/WorkflowsPane.tsx, src/workflow/gates.ts]
findings.action: Specify amendment presentation storage, consumption and approval integration, including compatibility with existing flat records. Include amendments/store.ts and its callers, or explicitly revise the claimed scope instead of promising AMD enforcement.

findings.premise: A presentation invalidated by rejection can recover through re-presentation without changing existing re-approval behavior.
findings.evidence: listPendingArtifacts excludes non-empty rejectedAt and approvedAt. The proposed recordPresentations accepts only pending artifacts, but §4 says a rejected presentation is withheld 'until re-presented'. That recovery cannot occur for a rejected record. Existing approveArtifactOwned deliberately clears rejection, and gates.test.ts verifies 'reject then approve clears the rejection'. The design supplies no reopen transition or compatibility policy. [files: src/workflow/pending.ts, src/workflow/gates.ts, src/workflow/__tests__/gates.test.ts, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103d5d33994/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Define a reachable recovery path for rejected and previously approved records before default-on rollout. Preserve the intended rangeBase semantics and test reject→re-present→approve.

findings.premise: This is a standalone Story without parent HLD contracts, and its simple presentation ownership relationship does not require an ERD.
findings.evidence: The persisted artifact has meta.standalone:true, sizeClass:'feature', hldAmendmentsApplied:[], and empty owned/consumed contract lists. The proposed optional embedded metadata establishes one current presentation per artifact, replaced on re-presentation and consumed on approval. Prose is adequate for that relationship. The JSON contains no companion references or structured visual definitions; there are no linked visual artifacts to inspect, and no rendered verification is claimed. [files: .insrc/artifacts/LLD-d5d33994ea4dee69-S001.json, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103d5d33994/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Keep the standalone boundary. Resolve the concrete cross-module compatibility gaps above; a sequence diagram would be optional once the interaction contract is complete.

findings.premise: An existing per-artifact approval lock can guarantee consistent presentation and approval writes for every artifact kind.
findings.evidence: approveArtifactByJsonPath returns directly through approveArtifactOwned when !build; only BUILD acquires withBuildWriter. Other artifact writes use writeAtomic, which writes a shared `${absPath}.tmp` and renames it without locking the read-modify-write transaction. Workflow methods run on session workers, so independent sessions can write concurrently. The claimed existing lock therefore does not protect non-BUILD token checks, consumption or presentation refreshes. [files: src/workflow/gates.ts, src/workflow/approval-owner.ts, src/workflow/storage.ts, src/daemon/threads/method-class.ts, src/daemon/threads/router.ts]
findings.action: Specify shared cross-worker ownership for presentation and approval writes on every supported kind, including final rereads and interactions with rejection/review writers. Test concurrent sessions rather than only sequential socket calls.

findings.premise: Invalid or ambiguous presentation names have one consistent, backward-compatible error contract.
findings.evidence: §2.1 specifies NotPendingError when any name matches zero or multiple pending artifacts and requires every name to resolve uniquely. The same function's return contract and §4 instead put those names in notPending without writing them. Existing handleInsrcPresent returns partial success for a mixed valid/invalid list, and present-dispatch.test.ts asserts that behavior. The design leaves these mutually different outcomes unresolved. [files: src/mcp/server.ts, src/mcp/__tests__/present-dispatch.test.ts, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103d5d33994/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Choose and document per-name partial success versus whole-call failure, including whether earlier stamps survive later write failures. Preserve the promised MCP response semantics and distinguish invalid names from persistence errors.

findings.premise: The existing gates and presentation suites can pass unchanged under the default-enabled requirement, as ac6 states.
findings.evidence: gates.test.ts::writeFixture creates metadata without presentation fields. Its approval test stamps only an other-party review before calling approveArtifactByJsonPath, which the new gate must reject. present-dispatch.test.ts's fake daemon returns the workflow.pending shape for every request and asserts a workflow.pending call; it cannot substantiate the new persistence contract unchanged. The planned integration cases also omit fingerprinted BUILD approval, amendment approval and existing client approval flows. [files: src/workflow/__tests__/gates.test.ts, src/mcp/__tests__/present-dispatch.test.ts, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103d5d33994/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Revise ac6's proving strategy to migrate fixtures and transport assertions while retaining explicit missing-presentation rejection tests. Add regression cases for fingerprinted BUILD, AMD, rejection recovery, client wiring and concurrent writers. Supply upstream criterion text to verify the remaining mappings fully.

summary.prose: Make the daemon itself refuse workflow approvals that were never presented to the human first. insrc_present becomes a write: it stamps a fresh, single-use presentation record (token + timestamp + session) onto each pending artifact. The shared approve path (approveWorkflowTarget -> approveArtifactByJsonPath in src/workflow/gates.ts, used by the MCP tool, raw IPC, the IDE review pane and the TUI) then requires that record for every artifact it approves — including overrides — and consumes it. epicHash batch approval must additionally name the explicit artifact ids it covers, so a blanket batch can no longer approve a whole chain. Review gates (block verdict, other-party, BUILD freshness) are untouched.

citations.quotedText: approveArtifactByJsonPath enforces review block + otherPartyReviewGap + BUILD freshness with overrideReview escape.
handleInsrcPresent changes nothing — reads pending, answers presented/notPending, records no presentation.
workflow.approve RPC accepts artifactPath or epicHash from any IPC caller and forwards to approveWorkflowTarget.
workflow.reviewDecision reuses the same approval seam for the IDE review pane.
handleWorkflowApprove validates exactly-one-of artifactPath/epicHash and forwards; holds no approval logic.
handleWorkflowPending is a pure scan of .insrc/artifacts (approvedAt absent AND rejectedAt absent).
approveWorkflowTarget resolves single path or epicHash batch and runs each artifact through approveArtifactByJsonPath into approved/skipped.
